turns.content: Someone I love once described my work as Dreams for the Dreamless. She said it almost casually, but it landed as true. It gave a name to the shape of my work: writing, coding, tools, games, and worlds that make the inside of my head accessible to people who cannot get there on their own. On bad days, when I doubt whether any of it matters, that phrase becomes a load-bearing beam. It reminds me that I am trying to build doors for people who have not been given language for what they feel.
That sounds less like a slogan and more like a mission someone helped you recognize.
Why does Dreams for the Dreamless matter to me?
